items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: On drumming we had Si Frasier, Josiah Frasier on drumming.

ctx.x: Now we formed a band ourselves.

And I don't want to make it too long but I'll tell you some of the members of the band. On drumming we had Si Frasier, Josiah Frasier on drumming. On bass we had Eddie Barrera. On piano we had Mercedes Fields. On the trumpet we had Bush Hall. Well Bush Hall died and he was replaced with Red Alam. He had Red Alam. He had Darius Ballera. Darius Ballera. Darius Ballera. Darius Ballera.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1972-01-19
items.q: Now that band that consisted of during them times, Red Island on Trump and Henry Red Island on cornet, Yank on trombone, Paul Bones on E-Flat Alto sax, and Eddie Johnson on tenor, and Mercedes Gorman

ctx.x: And the Pack House that was located on the court had the restaurant and ball and pool table downstairs. They called it, they was run by this fella by the name of Faubacher. And this fella, Bebe, William Ridgely's brother, he was the manager of the place. I think I don't know, remember his name? His first name? Yeah, his first name was Bebe Ridgely, his first name, he was a big tall, brown skin, heavy built man. But he was the manager of that place there, I can't think of his first name. But all I can tell you,…
What's the name of that band?

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: And we said we had Paul Bones, Eddie, Morrell, Lawrence Morrell

ctx.x: I mean any relation of the other halls like Edmund Hall and...

No, relations at all. Bush Hall. No, he had no relation at all. Let's see. We formed a...we first called the band the Golden Rule New Orleans Jazz Band, the Golden Rule Band. And we said we had Paul Bones, Eddie, Morrell, Lawrence Morrell, and we didn't have no piano during them days with the outfit. And later on, we formally made the band into the Young Tuxedo Band. Name it after Paul. That time it was called the Original Tuxedo Band with Bebe originally on trombone, which is the manager. And... Come right on…
